plainSummary: A delegated plan can claim a review that never happened and start work anyway.
summary: authority.break.test.ts runs4 tests:3 pass,1 fail. prepareExecutablePlan checks only truthiness of workstream.specBreakReviewId before creating a delegated seal; it does not load the review or verify approval/target/scope. Fabricated 3317ada5-b347-894e-8c88-110b7b42d58b/SR-does-not-exist bypasses requireSpecBreak:true.

findings.gap: New delegated snapshot path accepts arbitrary nonempty specBreakReviewId despite requireSpecBreak. A request grant plus nonexistent review string creates a seal and makes the plan executable.
findings.plainImpact: Agents can begin work without the independent spec review required by the plan.
findings.fixProposal: Resolve the referenced review and require a matching workstream spec approval with no unresolved blocking review; ensure review applies to the proposed revision rather than an older plan.

evidence.citedTest: packages/ledger/src/permission/authority.break.test.ts::does not accept a fabricated spec-review reference when a delegated plan requires review

residualRisks: Other tests cover scoped authority/revoke/deny and context correction identity. Review freshness and CLI no-context denial require follow-up regression after fixing this boundary.
